ledger.note: 1316: Amda Seyon brings Hadiya under Ethiopian control. "after conquering Damot, Emperor Amda Seyon I proceeded to Hadiya"; he "brought it under his control using Gura armies from modern Eritrea"; King Amano "refused to submit"; Hadiya "became an autonomous province of Abyssinia in the fourteenth century" while "historically a vassal state of the Adal federation" (undated). The Hadiya page gives no year for the campaign; 1316 is the ethiopian-empire dossier's (/ledger/3 gain, 1316/7), so the century is this page's and the year the sibling's. Mirror of that gain, which records an annexation; the page's 'autonomous province' wording would also fit a vassal_start, a form for af-01-b to settle (review repair 2026-10-19: the first draft had no event and drew Hadiya as sovereign 1250-1893).

"In the 1600s Hadiya regained its independence and was led by a Garad."; "defeated the troops of Emperor Susenyos I thus protecting their frontier from Abyssinian annexation for the next three hundred years". The page gives no year: 1632 is the end of Susenyos's reign (1606-1632, ethiopian-empire dossier) and a bridge. The parts the Oromo overran in the late sixteenth century ("some parts of the Hadiya region", no year or part named; the Hadiya people page: "In the late sixteenth century, the Hadiya regions were overrun by Oromo migrations"; the Oromo migrations page does not mention Hadiya) are not taken out. ethiopian-empire has no matching loss (it records the 1316 gain and a gain of Hadiya territory in 1889 from 'nobody').

wars.outcome: After conquering Damot, Amda Seyon "brought Hadiya under his control"; King Amano refused submission and the emperor "slew the inhabitants of the country with the point of the sword".

Hadiya was "historically a vassal state of the Adal federation" (undated) and stayed in the Zeila union. The Hadiya people page: Amda Seyon "slew the inhabitants of the country with the point of the sword".

wars.name: Hadiya revolts against Ethiopia
wars.outcome: Sarsa Dengel suppressed a revolt of Garad Aze at the Battle of Hadiya (1569); in the 1600s Garad Sidi Mohammed defeated Susenyos I's troops, "protecting the frontier for about three centuries".
wars.note: The 1569 date is from the title of the linked article (Battle of Hadiya (1569)), not from the page text. The Susenyos victory is undated on the page: 1632 closes the reign (1606-1632, ethiopian-empire dossier). The regain of independence is the ledger event of 1632.

notes:
New dossier: Cliopatria lacks Hadiya (the ethiopian-empire dossier of af-01-b uses the counterpart 'hadiya-sultanate' for its 1316 gain of Hadiya and 'nobody' for its 1889 gain; this page has Qabeena annexed from the Hadiya in 1889, so b's counterpart for 1889 should be hadiya-sultanate). One page opened (Hadiya Sultanate; budget 1-2). The page has no capital, no founding year (13th century), no Hadiya events between the 14th-century wars and the Oromo expansion, and it is inconsistent on Zara Yaqob ('late 14th century' for a reign usually dated 1434-1468). The Ethiopian suzerainty of the 14th century is a vassal relation that the Ethiopian dossier records; it is not repeated here because the Hadiya state continued. Gazetteer names needed: Hadiya (the Hadiya and Kembata country, southern Ethiopia). Capital coordinate is a stand-in.
Review repair (2026-10-19): (1) The 1316 loss to ethiopian-empire (mirror of its /ledger/3 gain) and a 1632 regain (confidence 1; "In the 1600s", no year on the page) split the life: Hadiya holds no land in 1316-1631 in this dossier (a gap between keyframes 0 and 1, so that the land is not drawn by both dossiers). The page's wording ("autonomous province", "vassal state of the Adal federation") would also fit a vassal tint; the form is for af-01-b and the orchestrator to agree. ethiopian-empire needs a loss of Hadiya to hadiya-sultanate in the 1600s (af-01-b), and its 1889 gain should name hadiya-sultanate, not 'nobody'. (2) The 1590 Oromo loss is dropped: the Hadiya state held no land then, and the page names no part ('some parts of the Hadiya region'); the Hadiya people page says only 'late sixteenth century' and the Oromo migrations page does not mention Hadiya, so the overrun date and extent stay unknown (thin item not resolved). (3) The 1889 and 1893 events now remove only Qabeena and the Halaba, as approximate coordinate discs (the gazetteer has neither; neither page gives coordinates, so about 8.2 N 37.85 E and 7.31 N 38.09 E are my approximations), and both are lowered to confidence 2. (4) The founding year stays a placeholder (the Hadiya people page too says only 'in existence by the 13th century'). Other facts on the pages not drawn: the 1689 claim of Khodja Murad that the Hadiya king had submitted to Abyssinia (Hadiya people page), Zara Yaqob's Hadiya tribute and the Adal-Hadiya wars (undated), Imam Ahmad's visit to Hadiya. Gazetteer names needed: Hadiya (region), Qabeena and Halaba (places).
